hook: SCP-3890 is written by the researcher who is trapped inside it, using the only format she knows: the Foundation report. It is split across several pages, so read them in order and watch the template itself. The later entries include heavy swearing, corpses and thoughts of suicide.
whyItMatters:
The article's main device is that the document format is a character. Containment procedures become survival rules, the description becomes a diary, and the headings keep appearing long after the person filling them in has stopped being able to.

It is also a strong memory-loss story told from the inside, where the reader notices what is missing before the narrator does.
thingsToNotice:
Dr. Elizabeth Graham lands in an endless desert of ruins full of blank, wandering people, and is hunted by a mimic that disguises itself as anything (a fly, a star, a speck of dirt on her leg) and eats memories. She works out that the wanderers are earlier victims, shelters in a bank beside a family who killed themselves, and keeps repeating her own name so she will not lose it.

The boy Tony who joins her turns out to be the mimic, and it leaves behind a report in her handwriting, so the garbled page just before, with her sentences shuffled into nonsense, reads very differently in hindsight. She finally kills it with a knife and the class becomes Neutralized, but its last attack leaves her leaking memory: she forgets the Titanic mid-sentence, decides she does not want to die, and the final page is an empty template.
